I am 54 years old and have been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. My family has 7 people and some of them work off-farm, so we have a bit of cash coming in, but we still rely heavily on what the land produces. I split my 8 mu into two parts: 6 mu for the wheat-maize double crop and 2 mu for cotton. The wheat-maize rotation is our staple — it feeds the family and gives us grain to sell — so I give it the most attention. For the winter wheat on those 6 mu, I will rotary till the land in early October and plant an improved variety like the ones my neighbors use. I will put down about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some phosphorus and potassium, because I have learned over the years that if I go too low on fertilizer, the yield drops badly and I regret it all year. I will irrigate three times — winter irrigation, one at jointing, and one at grain filling — because the well water is there, but pumping costs money so I do not waste it. I will spray pesticide twice, once for weeds and once for insects if they show up. After wheat harvest in early June, there is no time to waste; I will plant hybrid maize right away using no-tillage, which is what everyone here does. The maize will get about 16 kg N per mu and a couple of irrigations, plus two pesticide sprays. For the 2 mu of cotton, I will rotary till in April and plant an improved variety. Cotton needs a lot of spraying for bollworms, so I will spray about 12 times through the season, and irrigate three times. I expect about 450 kg per mu from the wheat, 500 kg per mu from the maize, and 250 kg per mu of seed cotton. I do not try to squeeze every last kilogram out — I aim for a safe, decent yield that I know I can achieve without breaking the bank on inputs.
